n: Chapter 33 is a turning point. Before news of Jerusalem’s fall arrives, God renews Ezekiel’s call as a watchman (compare 3:16–21). From here the book shifts toward hope and restoration.

f.w: Again the word of the LORD came unto me

n: When war threatens, a city chooses one of its own as a watchman to stand on the wall and look for danger.

f.w: set him for their watchman

n: If he sees an army coming, he blows the trumpet to warn everyone.

f.w: he blow the trumpet
f.g: The shofar, a ram’s-horn trumpet used to sound alarms.

n: Anyone who hears the alarm but ignores it is responsible for his own death.

f.w: his blood shall be upon his own head

n: He heard and did nothing, so his blood is on him. But anyone who listens saves his life.

f.w: he that taketh warning shall deliver his soul

n: But if the watchman sees danger and stays silent, people still die in their sins—yet God holds the watchman responsible.

f.w: his blood will I require at the watchman's hand

n: God has made Ezekiel that watchman for Israel. He must listen to God and pass the warning on. Latter-day Saint leaders and members are likewise taught to warn their neighbors with love.

f.w: I have set thee a watchman

n: If God declares a wicked person will die and Ezekiel doesn’t warn him, Ezekiel shares the guilt.

f.w: O wicked man, thou shalt surely die

n: If he warns and they don’t turn, Ezekiel has saved himself.

f.w: thou hast delivered thy soul

n: The exiles are now crushed by guilt: “Our sins weigh on us and we are wasting away—how can we live?” For the first time they admit their sin—and despair.

f.w: we pine away in them

n: God answers despair with hope: he swears he takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked but wants them to turn and live. “Turn, turn—why will you die?”

f.w: I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked
turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways

n: Past righteousness won’t save someone who turns to sin, and past wickedness won’t condemn someone who turns from it. What matters is the direction you are now facing.

f.w: he shall not fall thereby in the day that he turneth from his wickedness

n: If a righteous person trusts in his own goodness as a license to sin, his past good deeds won’t be remembered.

f.w: if he trust to his own righteousness

n: But if a wicked person turns from sin and does what is right…

f.w: if he turn from his sin

n: …returning collateral, repaying what he stole, and walking in the laws that give life, he will surely live. Real repentance includes restitution where possible.

f.w: give again that he had robbed
the statutes of life

n: None of his past sins will be held against him. He will live.

f.w: None of his sins that he hath committed shall be mentioned unto him

n: Some still say God isn’t fair—but it is their ways that are unfair.

f.w: The way of the Lord is not equal

n: A righteous person who turns to evil will die for it.

f.w: he shall even die thereby

n: A wicked person who turns to righteousness will live because of it.

f.w: he shall live thereby

n: God will judge each person by his own ways.

f.w: I will judge you every one after his ways

n: The long-awaited moment: in the twelfth year, a refugee from Jerusalem arrives and reports, “The city has fallen!” The journey from Jerusalem to Babylon took several months.

f.w: in the twelfth year of our captivity, in the tenth month
f.g: About January 585 BC, roughly five months after the city fell (some manuscripts read the eleventh year).

f.w: The city is smitten

n: The evening before the messenger arrived, God’s hand came on Ezekiel and opened his mouth. His years of restricted speech ended, just as God had promised.

f.w: I was no more dumb

n: God speaks to Ezekiel again.

f.w: Then the word of the LORD came unto me
f.g: His first message after the news of the fall.

n: Survivors living among the ruins in Judah boasted: “Abraham was just one man and he got the land; we are many, so surely it’s ours.” They claimed Abraham’s promise without Abraham’s faith.

f.w: Abraham was one, and he inherited the land

n: God replies: you eat meat with the blood in it, worship idols, and murder—and you expect to own the land?

f.w: Ye eat with the blood

n: You rely on your swords, do detestable things, and commit adultery—should you own the land? Covenant blessings require covenant faithfulness.

f.w: Ye stand upon your sword

n: Those in the ruins will die by sword, wild beasts, and disease—even in fortresses and caves.

f.w: the forts and in the caves

n: The land will be utterly desolate, its proud strength ended, its mountains empty of travelers.

f.w: the pomp of her strength

n: Then they will know the Lord, when the land lies waste because of their abominations.

f.w: because of all their abominations

n: Ezekiel has become popular. People chat about him by the walls and in doorways: “Let’s go hear what the Lord says today!”

f.w: talking against thee

n: They come and sit before him like devoted followers and listen—but they don’t do what he says. Their words are full of affection, but their hearts are set on gain.

f.w: they hear thy words, but they will not do them
with their mouth they shew much love

n: To them Ezekiel is like a singer with a beautiful voice performing love songs—enjoyable entertainment, but not something to act on.

f.w: a very lovely song of one that hath a pleasant voice

n: But when what he says comes to pass—and it will—they will know a prophet has been among them.

f.w: shall they know that a prophet hath been among them
